confidence: The Chinese Repository's Canton of 1835. Rice is the top of its range. No source gives Canton's cash a tael; its cash is by the dollar, about 1,000 cash (a Canton letter of 1837, and a voyager's round figure for the Guangdong coast in 1832), at 0.72 tael a dollar.

cash.note: About 1,000 cash to the dollar at Canton (Chinese Repository, 1837), so about 1,390 cash to the tael at 0.72 tael a dollar; empire-wide, 1,200-1,500 in 1836-1837

dollar.note: 0.72 tael (the GPIH files' rate, a later Beijing one); Canton's own 1835 figures bracket it at 0.71 and 0.75. Cents are hundredths

rice.label: historical
rice.note: Up to 3 taels a picul (100 catties of 0.6048 kg)

fish.label: historical
fish.note: Salted fish, 0.05-0.16 tael a catty, the midpoint

fuel.label: historical
fuel.note: Firewood, 0.1-0.18 tael a picul, the midpoint

wage.note: One mace (0.1 tael, about 14 cents) a day
